items.clauseName: Understanding the organisation and its context
items.requirement: Identify internal and external issues that can affect the organisation’s purpose, strategic direction and the intended results of the quality management system. Consider whether climate change is relevant, and keep the analysis current.

imported.evidenceExamples:
• SWOT or PESTLE analysis
• business continuity and resilience assessment
• records considering whether climate change is a relevant issue
• approved context and interested-party registers
• leadership workshop records and review minutes
• scope statement matched to actual sites, activities, products and services
• interviews confirming boundaries and responsibilities
• records showing significant contextual changes were acted on

lookFor: The analysis reflects the organisation’s real activities, markets, sites, workforce and operating environment
Both internal and external issues are considered
Climate change relevance is explicitly considered
The information is reviewed when significant change occurs
confirm: Issues identified can be traced into risks, objectives, scope or operational controls
Leaders can explain which issues matter and why
watchFor: Generic SWOT with no connection to the management system
Old analysis with no review evidence
Climate change marked not relevant without rationale

items.clauseName: Needs and expectations of interested parties
items.requirement: Identify relevant interested parties and determine the needs and expectations that the quality management system must address. Monitor changes, including relevant climate-related expectations.

imported.evidenceExamples:
• stakeholder map
• contracts, feedback, complaints and regulatory correspondence
• consultation records and review of changing expectations
• approved context and interested-party registers
• leadership workshop records and review minutes
• scope statement matched to actual sites, activities, products and services
• interviews confirming boundaries and responsibilities
• records showing significant contextual changes were acted on

lookFor: Relevant parties are identified, not just listed generically
Needs and expectations are specific enough to assess
Mandatory, contractual and voluntary commitments are distinguished
Changes are periodically reviewed
confirm: Requirements flow into legal registers, controls, objectives or communication arrangements
Workers, regulators, customers, suppliers and contractors are included where relevant
watchFor: Stakeholder list without requirements
No decision on which expectations the system must address
No evidence of review after business or legal change

items.clauseName: Scope of the quality management system
items.requirement: Define, maintain and make available the quality management system scope, considering context, interested-party requirements, products and services, sites and boundaries. Any requirement determined not to apply must be justified without affecting conformity or customer satisfaction.

imported.evidenceExamples:
• published management-system scope
• site and operational boundary map
• process map and justified applicability decisions
• approved context and interested-party registers
• leadership workshop records and review minutes
• scope statement matched to actual sites, activities, products and services
• interviews confirming boundaries and responsibilities
• records showing significant contextual changes were acted on

lookFor: Sites, activities, products, services and organisational boundaries are clear
Interfaces and outsourced activities are considered
Any non-applicability decision is justified where permitted
The written scope matches actual operations
confirm: Staff describe boundaries consistently
Certification, website and internal scope statements align
watchFor: Scope is broader or narrower than operations
Exclusion used to avoid a requirement that affects conformity
Missing sites, shifts, projects or controlled activities

items.clauseName: Quality management system and its processes
items.requirement: Establish, operate, maintain and improve the processes needed for the quality management system. Determine process inputs, outputs, sequence, interactions, controls, resources, responsibilities, risks, measures and the documented information needed for effective operation.

imported.evidenceExamples:
• approved context and interested-party registers
• leadership workshop records and review minutes
• scope statement matched to actual sites, activities, products and services
• interviews confirming boundaries and responsibilities
• records showing significant contextual changes were acted on

lookFor: The documented approach addresses every action and qualifier in the requirement
Actual practice matches the documented method
Responsibilities, criteria and retained records are clear
Implementation is current across relevant sites and activities
confirm: Interview, observation and records tell a consistent story
Controls achieve the intended result and are reviewed after change
watchFor: A template exists but has not been implemented
Evidence is isolated, outdated or not representative
No effectiveness check

items.requirement: Top management must be accountable for the quality management system, align it with strategic direction, integrate it into business processes, provide resources, promote process and risk-based thinking, support people, and drive intended results and improvement. Leadership should foster quality culture and ethical behaviour.

imported.evidenceExamples:
• approved policy and leadership communications
• organisation chart, role descriptions and authority matrix
• leadership meeting and management review records
• resource approvals and decisions
• interviews with leaders and workers showing responsibilities are understood
• observations showing leaders participate in relevant system activities

lookFor: Visible top-management ownership, decisions and resource allocation

Responsibilities are not delegated without oversight
confirm: Leaders can explain priorities, risks and intended outcomes
Meeting decisions are followed through
watchFor: Leadership evidenced only by a signed policy
System treated solely as the coordinator’s responsibility
No action where performance is poor
